key_insight: Generative AI can represent multiple plausible turbulent flows, but physical fidelity requires validation beyond visual realism, pointwise error, and low-order spectra.
engineering_relevance: Potential uses include stochastic closures, super-resolution, data assimilation, and uncertainty quantification for incompletely observed or unresolved flows.
method: Review diffusion, score-based, and related probability-transport models.
Examine flow generation, probabilistic reconstruction, reduced-order modeling, and temporal evolution.
Outline turbulence-aware validation and shared benchmark requirements.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports no quantitative performance results; it advocates evaluation of energy transfer, intermittency, conservation, temporal consistency, ensemble diversity, and generalization.
watch_item: Limited data, weak baselines, and incomplete physical validation can obscure failures and undermine reproducibility.
paper_title: Generative AI in Turbulence: Foundations, Applications, Validations and Benchmarks
